verdict.rationale: OpenRouter documents configurable model fallback: the `models` parameter takes an array of model IDs in priority order, and if the first model errors, OpenRouter automatically tries the next. It also falls back across providers by default, load-balancing to maximize uptime, and a community user confirms that fallback works by default without custom wrappers. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the per-request provider-level fallback settings (the `provider` object is described only as customizing routing), and hands-on reports of failover behavior under real outages.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can configure automatic fallback to another model or provider when one fails

citations.quote: Provide an array of model IDs in priority order. If the first model returns an error, OpenRouter will automatically try the next model in the list.
The `models` parameter lets you automatically try other models if the primary model's providers are down, rate-limited, or refuse to reply due to content moderation.
Fall back to other providers when one goes down.
You can customize how your requests are routed using the `provider` object in the request body
They also support fallback by default so you don't have to write wrappers.
